text: “FACES OF MARYLAND” SPEECH
label: body

text: Joint Session of the Maryland General Assembly
label: body

text: January 29, 2003
label: body

text: Senate President Mike Miller; Speaker Mike Busch; Members of the General Assembly;
label: body

text: Lt. Governor Steele; Chief Judge Bell; Judge Vaughan; Attorney General Joe Curran;
label: body

text: Treasurer Nancy Kopp; Comptroller William Donald Schaefer; members of Congress;
label: body

text: county executives and mayors; special guests; friends and fellow Marylanders:
label: body

text: What a tremendous honor it is to be standing before you today as Maryland’s governor.
label: body

text: I am so happy to be here – back with my friends in the Maryland General Assembly.
label: body

text: There are so many good, hard working people on both sides of the aisle – all eager to do
label: body

text: what’s right for the citizens of Maryland.
label: body

text: I served here for eight years – a tremendous experience for a young legislator.   I’ll
label: body

text: always cherish the time I spent here.
label: body

text: I made great friends and benefited from great mentors.  Many still serve in this body, and
label: body

text: others have joined my administration.
label: body

text: I experienced how the legislative process works, as well as the importance of principled
label: body

text: cooperation.
label: body

text: I observed and participated in serious debates about issues that matter to every citizen:
label: body

text: crime, drugs, education, healthcare, transportation, tort reform, the Chesapeake Bay, and
label: body

text: juvenile justice.
label: body

text: The Maryland General Assembly represents everything that a citizen legislature should
label: body

text: be: diverse, collegial, effective, informed and vigilant.  Serving here prepared me for the
label: body

text: challenges and demands of being an effective public servant.
label: body

text: To all the freshmen members of the Assembly, I encourage you to savor this experience.
label: body

text: I also encourage you to make the most of it.  You can do that by getting to know some of
label: body

text: the veteran members.  Neither party has a monopoly on talent in this legislature.
label: body

text: Many of the people in this room represent the best of public service:  I would like to
label: body

text: single out seven of these long-serving members today.
label: body

text: Together these members have won 126 races and served a total of 225 years in this
label: body

text: historic Assembly.
label: body

text: Please stand as I call your name.
label: body

text: Delegate Wade Kach: 28 years of service.
label: body

text: Delegate Joe Vallario: 28 years of service.
label: body

text: Delegate Hattie N. Harrison: 30 years of service.
label: body

text: Delegate John Arnick: 31 years of service.
label: body

text: Delegate Pauline Menes: 36 years of servic
label: body

text: e.
label: body

text: Senator Norman Stone: 40 years of service.
label: body

text: Senate President Mike Miller: 32 years of service.
label: body

text: It’s appropriate to celebrate public service, and the thoughtful people who choose to
label: body

text: serve.  They symbolize what is good and decent about this historic citizen legislature, and
label: body

text: we thank them.
label: body

text: Maryland continues to be an intellectual force powering the region.  We possess
label: body

text: exceptional institutions of higher education such as Johns Hopkins University and the
label: body

text: University of Maryland.
label: body

text: In the field of medical research, Maryland is an international leader, as demonstrated by
label: body

text: the world-renowned Johns Hopkins Medicine, University of Maryland Medical Systems,
label: body

text: and National Institutes of Health.
label: body

text: Further, NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and the National Aquarium in Baltimore
label: body

text: both speak to the state’s reputation as a science center.
label: body

text: The Port of Baltimore is world famous, and we are the center of the biotechnology
label: body

text: universe.
label: body

text: Our citizens are highly educated, and our per capita personal income is the sixth highest
label: body

text: in the nation.
label: body

text: As citizens of Maryland, we have a lot in which we can take pride.  Still, there are areas
label: body

text: in which we can do better.
label: body

text: We need to make our streets and communities safer.  According to FBI statistics,
label: body

text: Maryland continues to be one of the most violent states in the nation.
label: body

text: Further, the link between crime and drugs remains unbreakable.  A 2001 study performed
label: body

text: at Baltimore City’s central booking facility found that nearly three-quarters of arrestees
label: body

text: tested positive for at least one drug.
label: body

text: While the need for drug treatment programs is high, the need is not currently being met.
label: body

text: Presently, there are 7,500 taxpayer-funded treatment programs in Baltimore City, and an
label: body

text: estimated 55,000 people requiring treatment.
label: body

text: When it comes to the environment, there are challenges waiting for us, too.
label: body

text: Despite millions of dollars invested in environmental clean up, the health of the
label: body

text: Chesapeake Bay is precarious.
label: body

text: A 2002 study by the Chesapeake Bay Foundation found that the Bay’s health, which
label: body

text: scored 27 out of 100 in 1998, achieved the same low score in 2002.
label: body

text: You’ve heard me recite a number of statistics.  Statistics are serious business.
label: body

text: Sometimes, they can be downright scary.  But let me ask you to set them aside for a
label: body

text: moment, and consider the people behind the numbers.
label: body

text: Many of the issues facing us seem so difficult, so intractable, that we lose sight of the
label: body

text: human face associated with their challenges.
label: body

text: Sometimes we need to see – to touch – to feel – the real impact of these issues on the
label: body

text: lives of citizens in order to better understand them.
label: body

text: Sitting in front of you today are five individuals who help us put a “Maryland face” on
label: body

text: these issues.  Listen to their stories; they encompass so many lessons that can help us
label: body

text: achieve a better place to live, grow, work, and prosper.
label: body

text: First, I’d like you to meet Captain Bob Newberry.
label: body

text: Captain Bob is 45 years old and lives in Crumpton, Maryland.
label: body

text: He has been a Marylander since 1966, when his family moved to Queen Anne’s County
label: body

text: from Philadelphia.
label: body

text: Captain Bob has been a waterman since he was 15 years old.  For him, being a waterman
label: body

text: means “having something in your blood, and never hating to go to work.”
label: body

text: Today he fishes, crabs, harvests oysters, farms, and operates one of the few aquaculture
label: body

text: farms on the Eastern Shore.
label: body

text: Three years ago, he took on extra work as a part-time charter boat captain because it was
label: body

text: becoming more difficult to earn his livelihood through fishing.
label: body

text: New regulations have harmed his ability to do his job.  A significant drop in the Bay’s
label: body

text: oyster and crab populations are also threatening his industry.
label: body

text: Several years ago, the value of his average daily oyster catch was up to $2000.
label: body

text: Today, a typical catch falls within the $400 - $500 range.
label: body

text: He fears that next year’s oyster harvest will be the worst ever.
label: body

text: The blue crab is not faring much better.
label: body

text: Crabs have become increasingly difficult to catch since the 1980s.  The female crab
label: body

text: population has declined an estimated 80 percent since then, and the Chesapeake Bay
label: body

text: Foundation reports that the risk to the remaining population is “high and increasing.”
label: body

text: Captain Bob is not the only person whose livelihood has suffered as a result.
label: body

text: There are 7,000 licensed fishermen who earn their livelihood from the sea in Maryland.
label: body

text: They are responsible for an estimated 1 million pounds of harvest annually, representing
label: body

text: $86 million in annual income and 3,168 jobs.
label: body

text: Many feel that they have been unfairly blamed for the plight of the Bay.
label: body

text: They note that the poor water quality has killed off underwater sea grasses, leaving crabs
label: body

text: vulnerable to predatory fish.
label: body

text: They report that the oyster population is suffering because shells are not being
label: body

text: replenished.

label: body

text: on its banks.  They have an intimate appreciation of its beauty, its species, its problems,

text: and its vitality.

text: It is time to stop blaming them, and to start listening to them.

text: One day, in the not too distant future, there may be no fish, oysters, or crabs unless we
label: body

text: achieved measurable progress in cleaning up the Bay.  That means upgrading the 66
label: body

text: major municipal sewage treatment plants that cleanse its waters.

text: My capital budget makes a $95 million down payment in this area.  That’s a good start,
label: body

text: but we will clearly need additional resources to get the job done.

text: We will need to secure more dollars from the federal government in order to complete

text: The Chesapeake Bay is central to our identity.  It permeates every aspect of our

text: economic, ecological, recreational life.  Its health affects the livelihood and well being of

text: every Maryland family.

text: Now, I’d like you to meet Adela Acosta, principal of Cesar Chavez Elementary School in
label: body

text: Prince George’s County.
label: body

text: We’ve heard the phrase “no child left behind” in recent years.  Adela was the student
label: body

text: who simply would not allow herself to be left behind.
label: body

text: Adela was born in Puerto Rico, and later immigrated to New York’s Spanish Harlem.
label: body

text: When she enrolled in kindergarten at the age of five, she found it a very scary experience.
label: body

text: “A foreign language enveloped me,” she would later write. “English sounded like rocks
label: body

text: dropping in a river.  My teachers seemed to think that if they spoke to me in a very loud
label: body

text: voice I would understand what they were saying.”
label: body

text: Eventually, her teachers labeled her as learning impaired, and she was placed in a special
label: body

text: education class in first grade.
label: body

text: Fortunately, a social worker discovered her, and she was sent to St. Paul’s parochial
label: body

text: school.  There she learned the joy and power of reading as a means of comfort and
label: body

text: escape.
label: body

text: Her fortunes improved, but she faced other obstacles.
label: body

text: Her father – a heroin addict – became blind as the result of a beating by neighborhood
label: body

text: bullies.  Adela became his surrogate eyes, reading to him, tending to his needs.  In effect,
label: body

text: she became his teacher.
label: body

text: One day, she informed her eighth grade teacher that she wanted to teach one day.  The
label: body

text: teacher advised her to go into show business because – and I quote – “you people are so
label: body

text: good at it.”
label: body

text: Fortunately, Adela decided to follow her heart instead.
label: body

text: She went on to earn an undergraduate degree in Secondary Education from the University
label: body

text: of Kansas, and a Master of Science in Education Degree from the University of Kansas.
label: body

text: She has begun doctoral studies in Education Leadership at Nova Southeastern University
label: body

text: in Florida.
label: body

text: Today, the girl once dismissed as learning-impaired is a nationally recognized educator.
label: body

text: President Bush appointed her to the Commission on Excellence in Special Education.
label: body

text: And First Lady Laura Bush – a former teacher herself – named her a National Role
label: body

text: Model for Education Reform.
label: body

text: In 1999 she helped open Cesar Chavez Elementary School.  As principal, she presides
label: body

text: over a diverse student body:  47 percent Hispanic, 49 percent African American, and 4
label: body

text: percent white.   Ninety-nine percent of her students receive Title I funding.
label: body

text: The girl whose potential was once overlooked by her teachers is now looking out for new
label: body

text: generations of disadvantaged students.
label: body

text: Because of Adela, no child is left behind at Cesar Chavez!
label: body

text: Adela’s experiences as a student and an educator have taught her some important lessons.
label: body

text: She knows that social promotion policy only hurts kids and sends the wrong message to
label: body

text: taxpayers.
label: body

text: She knows that every student should compete on a level playing field, and that fully
label: body

text: funding the Thornton Commission’s recommendations is critical to her mission.
label: body

text: I agree with Adela.  That is why our budget increases education aid $242 million –
label: body

text: including $148 million under the Thornton formula.
label: body

text: She and I both support the establishment of another commission – Thornton II – devoted
label: body

text: to an examination of education policy in Maryland.  Lieutenant Governor Steele will lead
label: body

text: this important effort!
label: body

text: Finally, she supports a real charter school bill that will encourage competition in our
label: body

text: public school system.  Passing charter school legislation is one of my top priorities for
label: body

text: this session.
label: body

text: It is time for this Assembly to enact a charter schools bill with teeth – one that will give
label: body

text: disadvantaged students the opportunity to pursue their dreams.  I ask you to do so this
label: body

text: year.

text: Keith’s story is similar to those of tens of thousands of hard working Marylanders.  But

text: as well.

text: The mission’s innovative spiritual recovery program enables addicts to find the path

text: towards recovery, employment, and better life skills.

text: The results speak for themselves: program graduates have an 80 percent chance of being

label: body

text: Gun violence – domestic abuse – sexually transmitted disease – lack of educational

text: Now, let’s meet Michael Taylor.
label: body

text: Michael was born in Baltimore in 1958, and attended Hillendale Elementary School.
label: body

text: When he was 12 years old, he was placed in the Rosewood Center.
label: body

text: Michael spent the next three decades of his life locked away in institutions.
label: body

text: “While I was in Rosewood, I didn’t have my freedom,” Michael later said. “I couldn’t
label: body

text: decorate my room the way I wanted. I couldn’t call people on the phone without
label: body

text: permission.  I was not happy there.”
label: body

text: The cost of being institutionalized in Maryland for 30 years is conservatively estimated at
label: body

text: $1.6 million.
label: body

text: But we can’t calculate the cost it exacted on Michael’s quality of life.
label: body

text: Michael was released from Rosewood just four years ago.  He began working for the
label: body

text: “Living Free Campaign” and “Stand Up and Speak Out” – two groups that promote
label: body

text: freedom and empowerment for the institutionalized.
label: body

text: On April 16, 2002, Michael did something he had been waiting to do his entire life.
label: body

text: He moved into his very own apartment.
label: body

text: He calls his new apartment, located in Towson, his “Freedom Pad,” because nobody else
label: body

text: lives there.
label: body

text: As Michael gained his freedom, his life started to flourish.
label: body

text: He secured a new job with “Best Buddies of Maryland”.  His activism has earned him
label: body

text: awards from the State Independent Living Council, Baltimore County Commission on
label: body

text: Disabilities, and ARC of Maryland.  He also lobbies on behalf of the disabled, so many
label: body

text: of you may know him already.
label: body

text: Michael Taylor is an American success story.
label: body

text: He is a Maryland success story.
label: body

text: And he is a success story for any individual who faces obstacles and challenges in his
label: body

text: life.
label: body

text: He embodies the success and wisdom of our investment in community-based services.

text: My 2004 budget includes important programs that will help people in similar

text: circumstances live with independence, dignity, and self-sufficiency.  These include:

text: • $5.2 million for the Transitioning Youth Program to help youth with disabilities

text: graduate from school into productive living and working environments

text: • $6.9 million to fund the Developmental Disabilities Waiting List to get people the

text: • $3.1 million to respond to emergencies faced by families in crisis, such as when

text: an older parent caring for their adult child can no longer provide that care
label: body

text: • $16 million to increase the wages that personal care workers receive to assist

text: those with disabilities to ensure a high quality of care.

text: • In total, funding for community services for individuals with developmental

label: body

label: body

text: This is a new day in Maryland.
label: body

text: We must usher all Marylanders into the 21st Century by moving people out of institutions
label: body

text: and into communities, where they live, learn, work and thrive like everyone else.
label: body

text: It is time to give every Marylander the tools and opportunities to make their own choices.

text: Our last guest is not with us today.
label: body

text: Rio-Jarell Tatum was the son of John S. Tatum and Roxanne Servance.
label: body

text: They raised the kind of kid that would make any parent proud.
label: body

text: Rio graduated from Baltimore’s Polytechnic Institute’s rigorous A Course in June 2001.
label: body

text: At Poly, he was captain of the baseball and soccer teams.  People remember his blazing
label: body

text: fastball as well as seeming inexhaustibility on the athletic field.  Others recall his polite,
label: body

text: confident, self-assured manner.
label: body

text: But his academic prowess stands out the most.  He was a member of the National Honor
label: body

text: Society, earning an incredible 3.97 grade point average.  In September 2001 he entered
label: body

text: Penn State with a full scholarship.
label: body

text: On May 26, 2002, an armed robber shot Rio on a Baltimore street.  He died at Shock
label: body

text: Trauma.
label: body

text: I wish I’d had the chance to meet this exceptional young man.
label: body

text: The things that made a big difference in his life – sports, scholarships, and family – also
label: body

text: impacted mine.
label: body

text: Here is a kid who did everything right, yet still became a victim of the gun violence
label: body

text: sweeping our state’s largest city.
label: body

text: Rio’s story should be a wake-up call for all of us.
label: body

text: As long as gun-toting criminals roam our streets and communities, no one – not even the
label: body

text: best and brightest among us – is safe.
label: body

text: That is why it is time to bring Project Exile to Maryland.
label: body

text: During its first year in Richmond, Virginia, Project Exile cut violent crime in half.  It is
label: body

text: time we bring this successful program to Maryland, too.

text: Thank you, John Tatum and Roxanne Servance, for joining us here today.

text: These are just a few of the fascinating people I met during the journey that ultimately

text: brought Kendel, Drew, Michael, Andrea, and I to Annapolis.

text: As we go about the business of getting our fiscal house in order and making difficult

text: Maryland who depend on us to protect them from injustice – provide a cleaner

text: Of course, we will disagree at times – sometimes vigorously. But I am confident these

text: Modifier 59 (Distinct Procedural Service)
label: body

text: According to the CPT book, modifier 59 is described as being necessary to
label: body

text: describe a distinct procedural service.  This modifier should only be used to
label: body

text: show a distinct procedural service when a comprehensive/component
label: body

text: coding pair is billed.  Modifier 59 should not be billed to represent that
label: body

text: multiple services of the same procedure code were performed.
label: body

text: A comprehensive/coding pair occurs when one code is considered a
label: body

text: component procedure and the other code is considered a comprehensive
label: body

text: procedure.  These code pairs are frequently referred to as bundled codes
label: body

text: thus meaning the component code is usually considered an integral part of
label: body

text: the comprehensive code.  Therefore, in most instances the most
label: body

text: comprehensive code only should be billed and the component code should
label: body

text: be denied as rebundled or mutually exclusive.
label: body

text: Modifier 59 should only be used in conjunction with a
label: body

text: comprehensive/coding pair procedure when appropriately unbundling the
label: body

text: code pair.  This modifier 59 should not be billed with the comprehensive
label: body

text: code.  The component code can be unbundled, or allowed separately, in
label: body

text: certain situations.  If the two services are performed at two different times
label: body

text: of day or the services are performed in two different anatomical sites, then
label: body

text: modifier 59 can be submitted with the component procedure code.
label: body

text: In order to communicate the special circumstances of the
label: body

text: component/comprehensive code pair unbundling, diagnoses codes and
label: body

text: anatomical modifiers must be utilized as appropriate on the claim form.  In
label: body

text: some cases, it may be necessary to attach a copy of the Operative Report
label: body

text: to further explain the reason for the unbundling of code pairs.
label: body

text: Modifier 59 should never be used in any other circumstances and is
label: body

text: subject to post payment review.  If the services performed and billed for a
label: body

text: date of service does not include a coding pair described above, then
label: body

text: modifier 59 is not valid or appropriate.

text: ABSTRACT
label: H1

text: The increased performance and cost-eﬃciency of modern
label: body

text: multi-core architectures allows for packet processing imple-
label: body

text: mented in software instead of using dedicated hardware.
label: body

text: Such solutions provide large ﬂexibility as features can be
label: body

text: added at any time. The drawback of such systems are bottle-
label: body

text: necks which appear during the processing of packets at line
label: body

text: rate up to 10 Gbit/s. Hence, specialized high-speed packet
label: body

text: processing frameworks are needed to use the full potential of
label: body

text: commodity hardware. Diﬀerent research groups have identi-
label: body

text: ﬁed several limiting factors and proposed their own solutions
label: body

text: by implementing custom drivers and kernel modules. We
label: body

text: provide a survey-like introduction to three diﬀerent frame-
label: body

text: works: the Intel Dataplane Development Kit, netmap and
label: body

text: PF RING DNA. To understand the required background of
label: body

text: packet processing implemented in software, we explain the
label: body

text: mechanisms of modern network adapters and network stacks
label: body

text: by reference to Unix-based operating systems. In particu-
label: body

text: lar, we present and compare the diﬀerent techniques that
label: body

text: are used by those frameworks to make high-speed packet
label: body

text: processing feasible.
label: body

text: Keywords
label: body

text: commodity hardware, highspeed packet processing, Linux
label: body

text: network stack, Intel Dataplane Development Kit, netmap,
label: body

text: PF RING DNA
label: body

text: INTRODUCTION
label: H1

text: Through steady development the performance of commod-
label: body

text: ity hardware has been continuously increased in recent years.
label: body

text: Multi-core architectures have therefore become more inter-
label: body

text: esting to fulﬁl network tasks by using software packet pro-
label: body

text: cessing systems instead of dedicated hardware. As an exam-
label: body

text: ple, all Unix-based operating systems can accomplish net-
label: body

text: work tasks, as a full protocol stack that handles the packet
label: body

text: processing, is implemented. The advantages of high ﬂexi-
label: body

text: bility and lowered costs are contrasted with possible higher
label: body

text: performance and reduced energy consumption achieved with
label: body

text: specialized hardware [21, 16].
label: body

text: Unix-based Software routers are a good example of packet
label: body

text: processing done using commodity hardware. Features can
label: body

text: be rapidly deployed, whereas dedicated hardware would con-
label: body

text: sume extensive development cycles before being able to be
label: body

text: upgraded. The RouteBricks project has shown that software
label: body

text: routers are in general capable of reaching the same perfor-
label: body

text: mance that hardware routers deliver today [22].
label: body

text: In order to achieve the line rate of 1 Gbit/s and 10 Gbit/s
label: body

text: network adapters, the problems of common packet process-
label: body

text: ing software have to be identiﬁed. Various research groups
label: body

text: [21, 22, 23] have therefore created models to determine those
label: body

text: limitations by running tests for diﬀerent use cases.
label: body

text: They
label: body

text: come to the conclusion that standard software is not capable
label: body

text: of reaching the maximum performance for small packet sizes.
label: body

text: Hence, several projects developed frameworks for high-speed
label: body

text: packet processing using commodity hardware [24, 25, 26].
label: body

text: These frameworks replace or extend conventional concepts
label: body

text: by implementing their own driver and kernel level improve-
label: body

text: ments. Some of the concepts used by these groups are ex-
label: body

text: plained in this paper.
label: body

text: Other research projects created software solutions that spe-
label: body

text: cialize on speciﬁc tasks like bridging or routing. One exam-
label: body

text: ple is Open vSwitch [27], an OpenFlow switch that can fully
label: body

text: replace a hardware switch. An instance of the latter is Click
label: body

text: modular router [28].
label: body

text: The remainder of this work is structured as follows: in chap-
label: body

text: ter 2 we provide the background for packet processing us-
label: body

text: ing commodity hardware. In particular, we use the Linux
label: body

text: network stack as an example, to highlight the arising prob-
label: body

text: lems with high-speed packet processing in common software
label: body

text: implementations.
label: body

text: Chapter 3 presents the Intel Dataplane
label: body

text: Development Kit (DPDK) and explains the main concepts.
label: body

text: Then, chapter 4 compares the Intel DPDK with two other
label: body

text: packet processing frameworks, netmap and PF RING DNA.
label: body

text: Chapter 5 concludes this paper.
label: body

text: PACKET PROCESSING USING
label: body

text: COMMODITY HARDWARE
label: body

text: In this chapter we give an overview of a common software im-
label: body

text: plementation for packet processing using commodity hard-
label: body

text: ware. For this purpose we use the network stack of Unix-
label: body

text: based operating systems as an example. We will begin with
label: body

text: the tasks of the network interface card (NIC) that receives
label: body

text: incoming packets, followed by the Linux network stack that
label: body

text: implements the necessary dataplane functionalities and con-
label: body

text: clude with the transmission of the network packet via a NIC.
label: body

text: An abstract view of this process is illustrated in ﬁgure 1.
label: body

text: The resulting performance limiting factors that can be iden-
label: body

text: tiﬁed during the packet processing of this implementation
label: body

text: conclude this chapter.

text: Linux Network Stack
label: H2

text: The network stack processes each packet layer by layer [1, 3,
label: body

text: 4], starting with the network layer. At ﬁrst, basic checks, in-
label: body

text: cluding integrity-veriﬁcation and application of ﬁrewall rules,
label: body

text: are performed. If the packet is faulty it gets dropped, oth-
label: body

text: erwise it gets passed to the routing subsystem (6) in order
label: body

text: to make a decision whether the packet has to be delivered
label: body

text: locally to a userspace application or forwarded to another
label: body

text: host. This decision is being made based on the implemented
label: body

text: routing algorithm that ﬁnds the best match for the destina-
label: body

text: tion IP address of the packet in the routing table [1].
label: body

text: If this address equals one of the hosts locally conﬁgured ad-
label: body

text: dresses the packet has to be delivered locally and is handed
label: body

text: over to the transport layer. The Linux network stack pro-
label: body

text: vides a complete implementation of the TCP and UDP pro-
label: body

text: tocols. A more detailed description of this implementation is
label: body

text: given in [3]. After passing the transport layer the packet can
label: body

text: ﬁnally be delivered to the application. Using the socket API
label: body

text: [19] the data of the sk buﬀgets copied to userspace. Now the
label: body

text: application has full access to the data of the received packet
label: body

text: (7a). The same way an application in userspace can pass a
label: body

text: packet down to the network stack in order to transmit it (8).
label: body

text: Here, one of the main tasks is to determine the next hop and
label: body

text: corresponding interface for an outgoing packet. This is ac-
label: body

text: complished by looking up the destination IP address in the
label: body

text: routing table [3]. In the case of forwarding the packet (7b),
label: body

text: no processing of layers beyond layer 3 is needed. On the net-
label: body

text: work layer the main task is to decrement the TTL header
label: body

text: ﬁeld and, in case it reached zero, to drop the packet and
label: body

text: send a corresponding ICMP message [1]. Furthermore, san-
label: body

text: ity checks, ﬁrewall rules and fragmentation can be applied.
label: body

text: Afterwards the packet gets passed to the transmitting part
label: body

text: of the network stack, too (8).
label: body

text: The layer 2 processing does not diﬀer for forwarded and lo-
label: body

text: cally created packets.
label: body

text: Based on the result of the routing
label: body

text: lookup, the layer 2 address of the next hop has to be iden-
label: body

text: tiﬁed using for instance the Address Resolution Protocol.
label: body

text: After meeting these tasks a function of the NIC is called,
label: body

text: informing it to transmit the packet.

text: Performance Limiting Factors
label: H2

text: The Linux network stack is designed for general purpose
label: body

text: networking. It is not only able to function as a router, but
label: body

text: also supports various protocols on diﬀerent layers like IPv4
label: body

text: and IPv6 on the network layer or TCP and UDP on the
label: body

text: transport layer [3]. While this design choice is convenient
label: body

text: for running common applications for “normal” users up to a
label: body

text: rate of 1 Gbit/s, it rapidly reaches a limit when approaching
label: body

text: the 10 Gbit/s at which the operating system can’t handle
label: body

text: more packets and thus starts dropping them. The following
label: body

text: paragraphs list and explain some of the impediments which
label: body

text: are being addressed by the frameworks presented in sections
label: body

text: The identiﬁed bottleneck is the CPU. A CPU can only op-
label: body

text: erate a limited number of cycles per second. The more com-
label: body

text: plex the processing of a packet is, the more CPU-cycles are
label: body

text: consumed, which then can not be used for other packets.
label: body

text: This limits the number of packets per second. Therefore, in
label: body

text: order to achieve a higher throughput, the goal must be to
label: body

text: reduce the per packet CPU-cycles.
label: body

text: Another limiting factor is the usage of the main memory,
label: body

text: which can be further divided into three problems: per-packet
label: body

text: allocation and deallocation, complex sk buﬀdata structure
label: body

text: and multiple memory copies. The ﬁrst one occurs right af-
label: body

text: ter the packet has been received by the NIC as described in
label: body

text: section 2.1. For every packet a sk buﬀhas to be allocated
label: body

text: and later on, when the packet has been passed to user-level
label: body

text: or has been transmitted, deallocated again. This behaviour
label: body

text: leads to excessive consumption of bus-cycles - that is, CPU-
label: body

text: cycles spent transferring data from the main memory to the
label: body

text: CPU - by the CPU, causing signiﬁcant overhead. The sec-
label: body

text: ond problem arises from the eﬀort of the network stack to be
label: body

text: compatible with as many protocols as possible. Therefore
label: body

label: body

text: A third major problem is the context switching from user
label: body

text: mode to kernel mode and vice versa. Every time the userlevel-
label: body

text: application wants to receive or send a packet it has to make
label: body

text: a system call, causing a context switch to kernel level (and
label: body

text: later on back to user level). While this design improves the
label: body

text: resistance to system crashes as the application in user space
label: body

text: cannot use critical hardware functions, it consumes a huge
label: body

text: part of the CPU-cycles [16].
label: body

text: When using multiple CPUs the packet processing can be
label: body

text: slowed down because of so called spinlocks [17]. Those locks
label: body

text: are the Linux implementation of active waiting-mutexes and
label: body

text: appear on multiple occasions in the network stack. For ex-
label: body

text: ample, in order to transmit a packet two locks have to be
label: body

text: acquired, which protect the access to the NIC’s transmit-
label: body

text: ting queue [1], resulting in a bottleneck as possible parallel
label: body

text: processing of frames is negated.
label: body

text: All of the mentioned design choices make the Linux network
label: body

text: stack a good general purpose networking solution, but not
label: body

text: for applications that require high-speed packet processing.
label: body

text: Therefore, packet processing frameworks like the ones pre-
label: body

text: sented in the remaining chapters of this paper implement
label: body

text: techniques that try to resolve most of the mentioned prob-
label: body

text: lems.

label: body

label: body

text: Chapter 2 showed that there is indeed need for frameworks
label: body

text: that replace or extend the network stack to solve problems
label: body

label: body

text: der to achieve the maximum performance. This chapter will
label: body

label: body

text: ﬁrst released in 2012. First an overview of the framework
label: body

text: is given, afterwards the main implemented libraries are ex-
label: body

text: plained. This includes the libraries for queue management,
label: body

text: memory management and packet buﬀers. This chapter con-
label: body

text: cludes with an illustration of how to use the DPDK with
label: body

text: user-land applications and what the inherited problems are.

label: body

label: body

label: body

label: body

label: body

text: Further Libraries and Features
label: H3

text: Aside from the already illustrated libraries which are needed
label: body

text: to allow basic networking operations, the Intel DPDK also
label: body

text: has further libraries and drivers that provide specialized
label: body

text: functionalities.
label: body

text: The LPM library implements a table that allows longest
label: body

text: preﬁx matching (LPM), which is an algorithm used to for-
label: body

text: ward packets depending on their IPv4 address [1]. The main
label: body

text: functions are to add or delete a rule to or from the table and
label: body

text: lookup an IP address using the LPM algorithm. The best
label: body

text: ﬁtting entry is then returned. Based on this library an ap-
label: body

text: plication can be written to fulﬁl IPv4 forwarding tasks. The
label: body

text: same functionalities but for the IPv6 protocol are provided
label: body

text: by the LPM6 library [8].
label: body

text: Another library oﬀers similar functionalities by providing
label: body

text: hash functions. The hash library allows to do eﬃcient and
label: body

text: fast lookups in a big set of entries using a unique key[8].
label: body

text: This can then be used for ﬂow classiﬁcation, that is, map-
label: body

text: ping a packet to the connection, called ﬂow, it belongs to.
label: body

text: This is useful to match for instance TCP packets to their
label: body

text: connection and process all the frames together in the con-
label: body

text: text of this ﬂow.
label: body

text: A common procedure to achieve this
label: body

text: matching is to create a hash value of the 5-tuple of the IP-
label: body

text: and transport-layer headers (source and destination address,
label: body

text: protocol, source and destination port) [8].
label: body

text: The timer library provides the ability for functions to be
label: body

text: executed asynchronously, which can be used for example for
label: body

text: garbage collectors.
label: body

text: The timer can be executed with high
label: body

text: precision only once or periodically. It uses an interface of
label: body

text: the EAL or the CPU’s Time Stamp Counter to receive a
label: body

text: precise time reference [8].
label: body

text: The DPDK also includes poll mode drivers for 1 Gbit/s and
label: body

text: 10 Gbit/s network cards and several other emulated frame-
label: body

text: works like virtio or VMXNET3 adapter [8]. These provide
label: body

text: APIs to directly conﬁgure the device and access the receiv-
label: body

text: ing and transmitting queues without the need for interrupts,
label: body

text: comparable to the NAPI drivers.
label: body

text: Several more specialised libraries are also provided. See [8]
label: body

text: for a full list and detailed descriptions.
label: body

text: Using the Dataplane Development Kit
label: H2

text: The Intel DPDK provides all its libraries by creating the
label: body

text: Environment Abstraction Layer (EAL) [5, 7]. The EAL has
label: body

text: access to low-level resources including hardware and mem-
label: body

text: ory space and provides a generic programming interface that
label: body

text: is optimized for the hardware of the system, but hides the
label: body

text: environment speciﬁcs from the applications and libraries.
label: body

text: The supplied services include the loading and launching of
label: body

text: applications, reserving memory space in form of memory
label: body

text: segments as described in section 3.2.2 and trace and debug-
label: body

text: ging functions for instance for the logging of events [8].
label: body

text: Before being able to compile an application the Intel DPDK
label: body

text: target environment directory, which contains all libraries
label: body

text: and header ﬁles, has to be created. To compile an applica-
label: body

text: tion two variables must be exported: RTE SDK pointing to
label: body

text: the installation directory of the DPDK and RTE TARGET
label: body

text: pointing to the environment directory. The compiled pro-
label: body

text: gram can now be run by linking it with the EAL [7].
label: body

text: One has to keep in mind that the Intel DPDK only provides
label: body

text: a framework for basic operations that allow packet process-
label: body

text: ing at high speed. It does not provide any functionalities
label: body

text: like layer three IP forwarding, the use of ﬁrewalls or any
label: body

text: protocols like TCP or UDP that are fully supported by the
label: body

text: Linux network stack. It is the programmers responsibility
label: body

text: to build all the needed functionalities using the provided li-
label: body

text: braries. Thus, porting an application to the Intel DPDK
label: body

text: can be time consuming.
label: body

text: However, the development of applications is eased as many
label: body

text: example programs, illustrating the use of diﬀerent libraries
label: body

text: or features, are provided. Furthermore, the dpdk.org-project
label: body

text: tracks the Intel DPDK by not only listing recent patches, but
label: body

text: also contributing major enhancements provided through the
label: body

text: community [5]. The DPDK vSwitch [9], an improved ver-
label: body

text: sion of OpenvSwitch, is an example of an application that
label: body

text: is based on the Intel DPDK and achieves signiﬁcant perfor-
label: body

text: mance boosts [10].

text: netmap
label: H2

text: Netmap is a framework developed at the University of Pisa
label: body

text: by Luigi Rizzo within “The netmap project” [11]. It is de-
label: body

text: signed for fast packet I/O in a safe manner, implemented as
label: body

text: a kernel module, thus, running completely in kernel mode.
label: body

text: Netmap implements techniques to resolve three problems of
label: body

text: packet processing: the dynamic allocation of memory per
label: body

text: packet, overhead produced through system calls and multi-
label: body

text: ple memory copies [12].
label: body

text: The data structures of the netmap architecture reside in the
label: body

text: same memory region (illustrated in ﬁgure 8) which is shared
label: body

text: by all user processes. This makes the forwarding of packets
label: body

text: Figure 8: The structures of the netmap architecture
label: body

text: (image from [12])
label: body

text: between diﬀerent interfaces possible without a single copy
label: body

text: operation.
label: body

text: Furthermore, netmap uses its own lightweight
label: body

text: representation of packet buﬀers [12].
label: body

text: Those pkt buf -
label: body

text: structures are ﬁxed-sized and are preallocated before the
label: body

text: actual packet processing begins. Each packet buﬀer is ref-
label: body

text: erenced by the ring of the corresponding NIC. Addition-
label: body

text: ally, netmap rings are used to keep references to the buﬀers.
label: body

text: This is a circular queue that uses an array to store the in-
label: body

text: dices and other information of the packets. The last data
label: body

text: structure, called netmap if, contains important information,
label: body

text: like the number of rings, about an interface.
label: body

text: To reduce
label: body

text: per-packet processing costs, netmap provides batching tech-
label: body

text: niques. Also, a method called parallel direct paths is utilized
label: body

text: to solve the problem of serialization during the access of traf-
label: body

text: ﬁc [16]. Basically, a direct path from a receiving or trans-
label: body

text: mitting queue of the NIC to the application in user space
label: body

text: is constructed and being assigned to only one core.
label: body

text: This
label: body

text: supports Receive Side Scaling (RSS) [18], a technique to
label: body

text: distribute incoming network traﬃc to multiple CPUs. RSS
label: body

text: is supported by many network cards as it “relieve[s] bottle-
label: body

text: necks in receive interrupt processing caused by overloading
label: body

text: a single CPU” [18].
label: body

text: Despite using shared memory regions and keeping the struc-
label: body

text: tures in kernel context, a misbehaving user application can-
label: body

text: not cause the kernel to crash [12]. However, processes can
label: body

text: corrupt each others netmap rings and packet buﬀers. A pos-
label: body

text: sible solution for this problem is to distribute each ring to a
label: body

text: separate memory region.
label: body

text: The netmap framework supports a wide range of soft- and
label: body

text: hardware. Initially it was developed for FreeBSD operat-
label: body

text: ing systems, but a Linux-version has been completed [11].
label: body

text: With regard to NICs, 10 Gbit/s adapters using ixgbe-driver
label: body

text: or 1 Gbit/s adapters from Intel, RealTek and nVidia are sup-
label: body

text: ported. We found no documented restrictions for the usage
label: body

text: of CPUs from diﬀerent manufacturers [16].
label: body

text: Netmap uses standard system calls like poll() or select()
label: body

text: for synchronization and other purposes [12]. While this re-
label: body

text: duces the probability of the system to crash, the perfor-
label: body

text: mance may be reduced by additional context switches as
label: body

text: described in section 2.4.
label: body

text: To ease the employment of netmap, a library that maps libp-
label: body

text: cap calls into netmap calls is provided. Furthermore, some
label: body

text: functionalities like IP-forwarding are already implemented
label: body

text: [16]. Notable examples of applications that added support
label: body

text: for netmap are Click [28] and VALE [29].
label: body

text: [6], [12] using netmap and [16] using PF RING DNA (and
label: body

text: several other packet processing frameworks) show that they
label: body

text: are able to achieve the line rate of 10 Gbit/s even with 64
label: body

text: byte packets. Of course, this depends on the used hardware
label: body

text: and can be diﬀerent for other applications and use cases.
label: body

label: body

label: body

text: CONCLUSION
label: H1

text: In this paper we described the problems of high-speed packet
label: body

text: processing using modern commodity hardware. Using the
label: body

text: Linux network stack as an example, several performance
label: body

text: limiting factors have been identiﬁed.
label: body

text: The basic function-
label: body

text: alities of the Intel Dataplane Development Kit have been
label: body

text: explained in detail. Furthermore, this framework has been
label: body

text: compared with two other projects, netmap and PF RING
label: body

text: DNA, to illustrate some techniques that solve the described
label: body

text: problems.
label: body

text: Commodity hardware is a valid alternative to packet pro-
label: body

text: cessing using dedicated hardware as the software is always
label: body

text: conﬁgurable to suit the current problem in the best possi-
label: body

text: Seminars FI / IITM SS 2014,
label: body

text: Network Architectures and Services, August 2014
label: body

text: ble way. Several solutions have been created over the past
label: body

text: few years to achieve the best performance that the hard-
label: body

text: ware allows. While the presented frameworks diﬀer in their
label: body

text: respective implementations, they all try to resolve the core
label: body

text: problems of existing, widely distributed packet processing
label: body

text: solutions: per-packet allocation and deallocation, multiple
label: body

text: memory copies, restrictions to parallel processing through
label: body

text: locking mechanisms and context switching.
label: body

text: One has to keep in mind, that such frameworks are not de-
label: body

text: signed to fulﬁl everyday general purpose networking tasks.
label: body

text: Widely distributed and established solutions like the Linux
label: body

text: network stack will retain the upper hand in those scenar-
label: body

text: ios, as they support for instance a broad range of protocols.
label: body

text: When it comes to high performance packet processing, the
label: body

text: Intel DPDK, netmap and PF RING DNA have the clear
label: body

text: advantage. They are all capable of reaching the line rate
label: body

text: of 10 Gbit/s for a speciﬁc task. The ﬁrst applications like
label: body

text: the DPDK vSwitch or VALE are becoming more and more
label: body

text: popular as they function reliable at high speed.
label: body

text: However, packet processing frameworks like the Intel Data-
label: body

text: plane Development Kit or PF RING only support selected
label: body

text: hard- and software.
label: body

text: Furthermore, new problems arise for
label: body

text: the end-user that has to write an application, as all frame-
label: body

text: works provide diﬀerent APIs.
label: body

text: As some of those projects
label: body

text: have dedicated communities like dpdk.org, the problem of
label: body

text: porting applications to a speciﬁc framework can be eased
label: body

text: signiﬁcantly. Therefore, packet processing frameworks and
label: body

text: commodity hardware are the way to go for the future, be-
label: body

text: cause hardware is constantly evolving, allowing for increased
label: body

text: performance. The same trend must be maintained by the re-
label: body

text: spective sophisticated software to become widely distributed
label: body

text: and, thus, the de facto standard for packet processing.
